gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the AMS lite in the A1 mini Combo (the unit ChatGPT called 'best for colorful fidget toys') can't use TPU or TPE. Flexible fidgets therefore print from the external spool in one color only. The AMS lite also isn't compatible with the X1 or P1 series, so it can't carry over if a buyer later moves up to the P1S that the top-ranked guide recommends.
standout_why: I compared against 3dprintgearlab.com (rank 1), extruly.com (cited), aemind.com/3d-printed-fidget-toys (cited) and tomshardware.com (cited). 3dprintgearlab only says the A1 mini's 'Direct-drive extruder handles TPU reliably' and never mentions an AMS lite filament limit. Extruly says 'Avoid TPU for articulated joints' as print advice, and that 'four-colour fidgets are one-click jobs' with the AMS lite, but it doesn't say the AMS lite can't take TPU. Aemind gives TPU drying tips and makes no AMS compatibility claim. The Tom's Hardware page returned only its title, so I couldn't check it. None of these pages say that the AMS lite works with the A1 and A1 mini only and not with the X1 or P1.
decides: This confirms the A1 mini or A1 as the pick for rigid PLA fidgets: print-in-place gears, articulated dragons and spinners. It changes whether the Combo is worth the extra money. A shopper who mostly wants flexible or squishy TPU fidgets gets no multicolor benefit from the AMS lite and should buy the printer alone and feed TPU from the external spool. A shopper who might move up to a P1S later should know the AMS lite doesn't move with them. The finding doesn't separate the A1 from the A1 mini, because the same AMS lite works with both.
